5º de Primaria · Inglés

Future with going to

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Si ya has decidido que este sábado vas a ir a la piscina, ¿cómo lo dices en inglés?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

«This Saturday I'm going to go to the swimming pool.» Con be going to + verbo hablamos de planes que ya hemos decidido. Es como el castellano «voy a…»: I'm going to = «voy a», she's going to = «va a».

2

Aprende14 apartados

Para empezar: The big school project

On Monday, Ms Taylor gave the class some exciting news: «This term, we are going to make a school garden!»

Everybody cheered. Then they made a plan together.

«First, we're going to clean the old corner behind the gym,» said Ms Taylor. «Who has ideas?»

Hugo raised his hand. «I'm going to bring my grandad's tools. He's a farmer and he's going to help us on Saturday.»

«My sister and I are going to make labels for the plants,» said Ainhoa.

«And I'm going to draw a map of the garden,» added Iker, who loved drawing.

Ms Taylor wrote everything on the board. «What are we going to plant?» she asked.

«Tomatoes!» «Strawberries!» «Sunflowers!» shouted the children.

Suddenly, Daniela looked out of the window. The sky was very dark. «Oh no! Look at those clouds. It's going to rain!»

«Don't worry,» laughed Ms Taylor. «Rain is good news for gardens. I think it will be the best project of the year.»

(Fíjate: going to sirve para planes ya decididos y para predicciones con pruebas, como las nubes. Will aparece al final para una opinión: «I think it will…».)

1. Plans for the future

We use be going to + verb to talk about plans and intentions: things we have already decided to do. «I'm going to visit my cousins this weekend.» «We're going to paint the kitchen.» «My sister is going to learn to play the guitar.»

It is very similar to Spanish: «voy a visitar», «vamos a pintar», «va a aprender». En castellano también usamos «ir a» para el futuro, así que es fácil de entender. Lo importante es no olvidar el verbo to be delante.

2. How to form it

The form has three parts: am / is / are + going to + verb (base form). «I am going to read.» «You are going to win.» «He is going to cook.» «We are going to travel.» «They are going to dance.»

In speaking we use the short forms: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're going to. The verb after to never changes: «She's going to play» (not «plays» or «played»).

Vídeo: Simple future with be going to · Ellii (formerly ESL Library) (YouTube) · 800 mil visualizaciones

3. Pronunciation: gonna

When people speak quickly in English, going to often sounds like «gonna» /gona/: «I'm gonna watch a film.» «Are you gonna come?» You will hear it in songs, films and series all the time.

But be careful: gonna is only for informal speaking. When you write, always write the complete form: going to. In exams, in emails to teachers and in your school work, never write «gonna».

Also notice the contractions with the verb be, which are normal in speaking and in informal writing:

  • I am → I'm going to…
  • you are → you're going to…
  • he is / she is / it is → he's / she's / it's going to…
  • we are / they are → we're / they're going to…

When go is the main verb, we can say «I'm going to go to the beach», but it's more natural to say «I'm going to the beach» (present continuous).

Practise with this chant: «What are you gonna do? I'm gonna dance! What is she gonna do? She's gonna go to France!»

4. Negatives

For the negative add not after am, is or are: «I'm not going to watch TV tonight.» «She isn't going to come to the party.» «We aren't going to take the bus; we're going to walk.»

Short forms: I'm not, he isn't / he's not, they aren't / they're not. Remember: we don't use don't or doesn't with going to. ✘ «I don't going to…» ✔ «I'm not going to…».

5. Questions and short answers

For questions we put am / is / are first: «Are you going to play tomorrow?» «Yes, I am.» / «No, I'm not.» «Is it going to rain?» «Yes, it is.» / «No, it isn't.»

With question words: «What are you going to do this summer?» «Where is he going to stay?» «When are they going to arrive?» «Who is going to bring the ball?» These questions are perfect to ask friends about their plans for the weekend or the holidays.

6. Future time expressions

With going to we often use future time expressions: tonight (esta noche), tomorrow (mañana), tomorrow morning, the day after tomorrow (pasado mañana), this weekend, next week (la semana que viene), next month, next year, in two days (dentro de dos días), soon (pronto).

«Next year I'm going to be in sixth grade.» «I'm going to call you tomorrow.» Ojo: tomorrow es «mañana» (el día siguiente), pero «por la mañana» es in the morning.

7. Intentions and resolutions

At the beginning of a new year, or a new school year, many people make resolutions (propósitos): things they want to change or improve. We usually write them with going to:

  • «This year I'm going to read a book every month.»
  • «I'm going to learn to swim.»
  • «I'm going to eat more fruit and fewer sweets.»
  • «I'm not going to spend so much time with the tablet.»
  • «I'm going to help more at home.»

Good resolutions are realistic and concrete. «I'm going to be perfect» is not a good resolution! «I'm going to practise the guitar for twenty minutes every day» is much better: you can check if you do it.

To make your resolutions stronger, add how and when: «I'm going to read every night before bed.» «I'm going to tidy my room on Saturday mornings.»

You can also talk about the resolutions of other people: «My dad is going to stop drinking so much coffee.» «My sister is going to join a theatre group.»

Write your resolutions on a card and check them at the end of the term. Did you do what you planned?

8. Predictions: look at the sky!

We also use going to for predictions when we can see that something is about to happen: there is evidence now. «Look at those black clouds! It's going to rain.» «Be careful! That glass is going to fall.» «Our team is winning 4-0. We're going to win!»

We see the signs, so we are quite sure. En castellano: «¡Cuidado, que se va a caer!». Es exactamente la misma idea.

9. Will or going to?

English has two common ways to talk about the future: going to and will. Here's how to choose:

  • Going to for plans already decided: «I'm going to visit Paris next summer. We've got the tickets.» And for predictions with evidence (something we can see now): «Look at that glass! It's going to fall.»
  • Will for decisions made at the moment of speaking: «It's cold in here.» – «I'll close the window.» And for predictions based on opinion, often with I think, maybe, probably: «I think it will be sunny tomorrow.» «Maybe robots will do our homework in the future.»
  • Will also for promises and offers: «I'll help you with your project.» «I won't tell anybody. I promise!»

Forms of will: will + base form for all persons: I will (I'll) go, she will (she'll) go. Negative: won't (will not). Question: «Will you come?» – «Yes, I will.»

Compare: «The phone is ringing!» – «I'll answer it.» (decided now) / «I'm going to call Grandma tonight.» (a plan from before).

Vídeo: Futuro simple (Going to vs. Will) · Learn English on Skype (YouTube) · 643 mil visualizaciones

10. Going to or present continuous?

Sometimes we use the present continuous for future plans that are fixed, with a time and a place: «I'm meeting Ana at five.» «We're flying to London on Friday» (we've got the tickets).

With going to we focus on the decision or intention: «I'm going to study harder this term.» At your level, going to is the safest choice for plans. In informal speech, native speakers often say «gonna»: «I'm gonna win!» It's OK in songs and chats, but in your writing use going to.

11. Reading: summer plans

Read Gael's message: «Hi Luca! School finishes in two weeks and I've got big plans. First, my family and I are going to spend July in Cantabria. We're going to stay in a cottage near the sea. My dad is going to teach me to surf! My little brother isn't going to surf; he's going to build sandcastles. In August I'm going to go to a science camp. We're going to make robots. Are you going to come to the village this year? Write soon! Gael.»

Where are they going to stay? What is Gael's dad going to do? What is Gael going to make at the camp?

12. Let's practise: my plans

Make a plans calendar for next week. Write one plan for each day: «On Monday I'm going to finish my project. On Tuesday I'm going to go to basketball…». Then compare with a partner: «Are you going to do anything on Wednesday?» «What are you going to do at the weekend?»

Second activity: New school year resolutions. Write three things you are going to do and two things you aren't going to do: «I'm going to read more. I'm not going to forget my homework.» Repaso: am/is/are + going to + verbo; negativa con not; pregunta empezando por am/is/are.

13. When I grow up…

What are you going to be when you grow up? Here is some vocabulary about jobs:

  • Health: doctor, nurse, vet (veterinario), dentist.
  • Science and technology: scientist, engineer, programmer, astronaut.
  • Art and entertainment: artist, musician, actor / actress, writer, photographer.
  • Services: teacher, firefighter (bombero), police officer, pilot, cook / chef, farmer.
  • Sport: footballer, tennis player, coach (entrenador).

Remember to use a / an with jobs: «I'm going to be a vet.» «She's going to be an engineer.» In Spanish we don't use the article («voy a ser veterinario»), but in English it's necessary!

Explain your reasons with because: «I'm going to be a vet because I love animals.» And talk about the steps: «First, I'm going to study biology. Then I'm going to work in a zoo.»

Of course, you can change your mind many times. Most adults didn't know at your age!

14. Writing: an invitation

An invitation is a short text to invite people to an event: a birthday party, a school play, a sports match… Here's how to write one:

  1. Greeting: «Dear Lucas,» or «Hi everybody!»
  2. The event with going to: «I'm going to have a birthday party!» «Our class is going to perform a play.»
  3. The details: when (date and time), where (place and address) and what you're going to do. «It's on Saturday 15th May, at 5 o'clock, at my house (12 Rose Street). We're going to play games, eat pizza and watch a film.»
  4. What to bring (if necessary): «Please bring a swimsuit and a towel.»
  5. Asking for an answer: «Please tell me if you can come before Wednesday.» Sometimes invitations say RSVP (from French: répondez s'il vous plaît, «please reply»).
  6. Closing: «Hope to see you there!» «See you soon,» + your name.

To answer an invitation: «Thank you for the invitation! I'd love to come.» or «Thank you, but I'm sorry, I can't come. I'm going to visit my grandparents that weekend.»

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Write a plan: «we / visit / the zoo / on Sunday»

  1. We → are (we're).
  2. are + going to + visit.

Resultado: We're going to visit the zoo on Sunday.

Ejemplo 2. Make it negative: «He's going to play tennis.»

  1. is + not → isn't.
  2. El resto no cambia.

Resultado: He isn't going to play tennis.

Ejemplo 3. Make a question with what: «They're going to cook pizza.»

  1. What + are + they + going to + cook?

Resultado: What are they going to cook?

Ejemplo 4. Going to or will? «Look! That boy ___ fall off the wall.» / «I'm thirsty.» «I ___ get you some water.»

  1. There is evidence (we can see him) → going to: is going to fall.
  2. Decision at the moment of speaking → will: I'll get.

Resultado: That boy is going to fall off the wall. I'll get you some water.

Ejemplo 5. Correct: «I'm going to be vet because I love animals.»

  1. Jobs need a / an in English.
  2. Vet starts with a consonant sound → a.

Resultado: I'm going to be a vet because I love animals.

Errores típicos

  • Olvidar el verbo to be: «I going to swim» → «I'm going to swim».
  • Cambiar el verbo después de to: «She's going to plays» → «She's going to play».
  • Hacer la negativa con don't: «I don't going to» → «I'm not going to».
  • No invertir en la pregunta: «You are going to come?» → «Are you going to come?».
  • Escribir «gonna» en un texto formal: mejor «going to».
  • Escribir «gonna» en un texto escrito: en la escritura siempre «going to».
  • Olvidar el artículo con las profesiones: «I'm going to be teacher» → «a teacher».

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Write the contractions: I am, she is, we are, they are.

    Ver solución
    I'm, she's, we're, they're.

  2. Complete with will: «I'm cold.» «I ___ close the window.»

    Ver solución
    'll (will).

  3. Write two resolutions for this school year.

    Ver solución
    Example: I'm going to read more. I'm going to learn to swim.

  4. Translate: «Voy a ser bombero.»

    Ver solución
    I'm going to be a firefighter.

  5. What does RSVP mean?

    Ver solución
    Please reply (répondez s'il vous plaît).

Nivel medio

  1. Complete: «I ___ going to watch a film tonight.»

    Ver solución
    am ('m).

  2. Complete: «My parents ___ going to buy a new car.»

    Ver solución
    are.

  3. Complete: «It ___ going to snow tomorrow.»

    Ver solución
    is.

  4. Make it negative: «We're going to stay at home.»

    Ver solución
    We aren't going to stay at home.

  5. Make a question: «She's going to sing.»

    Ver solución
    Is she going to sing?

  6. Answer: «Are you going to play football?» (yes)

    Ver solución
    Yes, I am.

  7. Prediction: there are black clouds. Write a sentence.

    Ver solución
    It's going to rain.

  8. Correct: «They going to visits London.»

    Ver solución
    They're going to visit London.

  9. Translate: «La semana que viene vamos a ir al museo.»

    Ver solución
    Next week we're going to go to the museum.

  10. Write three plans for next summer.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I'm going to swim every day. I'm going to read three books. We're going to visit my aunt.

  11. Going to or will? «I think robots ___ do housework in the future.»

    Ver solución
    will.

  12. Going to or will? «We've got the tickets. We ___ fly to Rome in July.»

    Ver solución
    are going to.

  13. Make negative: «She's going to be a pilot.»

    Ver solución
    She isn't going to be a pilot.

  14. Write a promise with will.

    Ver solución
    Example: I'll help you with your homework.

  15. Make a resolution more concrete: «I'm going to be healthier.»

    Ver solución
    Example: I'm going to eat fruit every day and walk to school.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Write an invitation to your birthday party with all the parts.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  2. Write a paragraph: «When I grow up, I'm going to be…» with reasons and steps.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  3. Write a short dialogue with two offers or decisions with will and two plans with going to.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  4. Write five predictions about your town in 2050 with will.

    Ver solución
    Open answer. Example: There will be more electric cars.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeOur class event

La clase organiza en inglés un evento (una feria, una obra o una jornada deportiva) y prepara el plan y las invitaciones.

Pasos

  1. Decide the event in groups and write the plan: who is going to do what.
  2. Make predictions: What's going to be difficult? What do you think will happen?
  3. Write invitations for families or another class with all the details.
  4. Hold the event and, afterwards, talk about what went well.

Producto final: Un plan de evento e invitaciones en inglés.

Cómo se valora

  • Uses going to for plans and predictions with evidence.
  • Uses will for decisions, opinions and promises.
  • Writes a complete invitation.
  • Talks about future intentions and jobs.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • El domingo, planificad la semana en inglés: «On Monday I'm going to…».
  • Haced juntos predicciones mirando el cielo o un partido: «It's going to rain», «They're going to win».
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Expresión de planes, intenciones y predicciones; futuro con be going to; expresiones temporales de futuro (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • Calendario de planes de la semana compartido en parejas.
  • Propósitos de curso escritos con going to.
  • Juego de predicciones con imágenes: «What's going to happen?».

Revisado el 22 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Talk about plans and intentions with going to (planes)
  • Form affirmative, negative and question sentences
  • Make predictions from what we can see
  • Use future time expressions: tomorrow, next week, this weekend
  • Choose between going to and will
  • Talk about intentions, resolutions and future jobs
  • Write an invitation to an event

Palabras clave

going to · am / is / are going to · isn't going to · Are you going to…? · plan · intention · prediction · tomorrow · next week · this weekend · gonna

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
